messages:
maya: quick heads-up — ran a KV cache hit-rate sweep on canary and results are kinda bad. overall prefix hit-rate ~12% (expected ~45%). attached sample of counts and a short profiler dump.

maya: sample (top-1k prompts):
```
prefix,requests,hits,hit_rate
"support: reset password",1200,198,0.165
"compose: subject:" ,980,85,0.087
"summarize: doc:" ,720,40,0.056
"chat: system:" ,410,350,0.854
```
maya: interestingly system prompts have high hit-rate but user-composed prefixes are all over the place. profiler shows a lot of wasted KV lookups + many small batches caused by kernel selection switching (small-seq vs long-seq) mid-request.

maya: question: how much do we want SDK-level cache opt-in vs server-side heuristics? also streaming + retry behavior seems to be bypassing cache keys (client retries re-issue without cache header).

jon: good catch. i think two separate problems: 1) cache keying granularity (we're including full metadata blob in key) -> explosion of keys, 2) client retries/streaming replays not preserving cache control.

jon: for (1) we should normalize keys to canonicalized prefix tokens + model+truncate-length. drop session-id/user-agent noise. for (2) add a short-lived request-id header that the proxy uses to dedupe streaming retries, and ensure SDK preserves cache headers across reconnects. :+1:

sam: agree w/ normalization. also batching: kernel selection toggles batches into different exec lanes which fragments KV warmup. propose batching heuristic: group by "cache-key-bucket" in scheduler before kernel-pick, then choose kernel per-bucket. that should increase warmup locality.

sam: small pseudo for SDK opt-in config:
```
// JS SDK
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: KEY, cache: { mode: 'opt-in', preserveOnRetry: true } })
await client.generate({ prompt: 'compose: subject: ...', cacheKey: 'prefix:compose:subject' })
```
sam: if mode is opt-in, server ignores cache headers unless backed by token-scoped permission. keeps default safe.

liu: perf regression data from canary after kernel selection change (yesterday):
```
metric,baseline,canary,delta
90p_latency_ms,120,175,+46%
p95_latency_ms,200,315,+57%
tokens_per_second,4200,3200,-24%
kv_hit_rate,0.42,0.12,-71%
```
liu: looks like the new kernel gating moves midsize requests to long-seq runner which has slower path for small batch sizes. plus cache fragmentation.

maya: thanks. we should probably revert kernel gating to previous rule while we iterate on keying & scheduling. i'm worried about streaming edge-case where client reconnects cause duplicate partial streaming that bypasses cache - that makes warmup ineffective.

jon: we can add a header `X-RW-Cache-Mode: opt-in|opt-out|inherit` and `X-RW-Cache-Key: <normalized>` to the API. proxy will honor header only if SDK-signed token present (prevents random clients from poisoning cache).

sam: also propose a server-side warmup job that samples top-N prefixes per workspace and preloads KV for current model variant on boot — lazy but scheduled. simple cron: daily top-1000 per workspace. could be gated on dedicated customers.

maya: small edge: streaming + chunked responses — if a stream starts and the client disconnects, we currently mark the request as failed and don't set cache entries. instead: if reconnect uses same request-id within 30s, treat as same request and only mark fill-to-cache once final chunk acknowledged. ops needs to audit cache semantics.

ops-bot: deploybot: canary-deploy/rv-kernel-gating reverted to 2026-03-10@02:14 (triggered by eng-runtime-alert). See: https://deploys.internal/redwood/rv-kernel-gating

liu: can we add a short experiment: 1) normalize keys (drop headers blob), 2) scheduler group-by cache-bucket, 3) SDK opt-in header preserved on retries. run on 5% traffic for 24hrs and compare.

jon: +1. i'll draft a PR for key canonicalization and header spec. sam can own scheduler change. maya will coordinate SDK header + docs. liu run perf jobs and dashboards.

sam: one more note — rate limiting: if SDK opt-in allows more cache writes, we should throttle fill-writes per workspace to avoid stampedes. simple token-bucket per workspace.

maya: sounded good. i'll open a tracking issue and callback this thread when PRs land. thanks all. :eyes:
